body: Why is the lower texture map so much darker than the rest of the textures?!

@saleeo Hello, in which Engine/Renderer have you tried the model? Does it look different than the sketchfab render?
If it's in Unreal, this could be an issue with the metallic map, as the lower is the only plastic part in the model.
If it's in Blender, there's been a change with the normal map node (new sub filtering option) that could create issue with the normals of the model making it darker then it actually is.
If you take a look at the lower, it's a very grainy plastic and I had issues in blender with those in the past.

@amadions
The texture you download IS darker than all the rest not sure why, it is the texture that colors the middle portion of the handgun.

I double checked with my local textures, and they look identical.
It is indeed darker than the texture of the upper and every other part of the gun but that's because it's the only part that's plastic, the other ones are metallic.

This material information is stored in the metallic map, I believe in Unreal the metalic map can sometimes be wrongfully set up as the roughness map which would create an issue in the final render of the object.

Can you tell me about which software are you trying to open this asset with ? I could hopefully help

@amadions
Hello there, thanks for the interest in helping out.
We were planning on making this gun a main weapon for one of our comic characters but as I said - the middle portion texture is darker than all the rest of the gun.
We can see this in the Unity3D program.

@saleeo Hi, Sorry to not being able to help much, I know that importing textures in an engine can be quite finicky, and I just don't know enough about Unity.
In my own testing on Unreal, I got an issue with the weapon looking darker and much more shinier than expected as Unreal sets specular lighting to a value of 0.5 by default which is way to high, and this was improved when lowering it down to 0.02 or something quite lower.

I hope you can find the issue, if not as a last resort I would suggest asking an LLM such as 'Perplexity'  for some advice on this topic, it has helped me with some issues in Unreal, I would expect it to help with Unity.

Best of luck.
